name: Van Leeuwen Ice Cream
notes: Restaurant's own site (vanleeuwenicecream.com) reused one generic order.online link (business/-33134) across ALL chain locations nationwide (verified: identical link on NYC, La Jolla, and other listings) — that generic link resolves to a non-location-specific landing page. Correct branch-specific order.online store URL found via Serper search on the physical address (4301 La Jolla Village Dr, Westfield UTC) and confirmed matching. Menu extracted from the store's Next.js RSC flight payload (self.__next_f.push), which double-escapes JSON; brace-balancing and regex extraction both failed on the escaping, so items were parsed via literal indexOf field-slicing (74 MenuPageItem markers, 73 parsed with name+price). Removed 1 'Most Ordered' carousel summary node (not a real item) and 9 section-header pseudo-entries whose 'price' field spuriously inherited the first nested item's price (Scoops, Sundaes, Milkshakes & Floats, Cookies & Treats, Classic/Vegan/Special 14 oz Pints, Drinks & Retail, Party Packs). Deduped cross-listed items appearing under both a normal section and Party Packs/Most Ordered (Rainbow Sprinkles, Original Hot Fudge Jar, and several Most-Ordered-carousel duplicates) by name+price, keeping first occurrence. 51 final dishes across 9 sections. Ran the markup/divisor sweep (1.00-1.35): no single divisor was clearly dominant (1.13 and 1.28 scored marginally higher than 1.00 on a loose 'clean price ending' heuristic with only 51 data points, likely noise since VL's own pricing already uses varied endings like .15/.20/.95/.75); treating prices as extracted (divisor 1.00) since this is the brand's own first-party order.online storefront, not a third-party marketplace app where baked-in delivery markups are the norm.
